rationale: Round 0 built and ran cleanly with no ICE, so this candidate shifts weights toward stronger obfuscation while throttling the passes that hurt most on this profile: exptree is a tiny (2639 text bytes, 14 functions), recursion-heavy benchmark (recSearch/doSearch/queens-style backtracking), so hot recursive loops are sensitive to control-flow overhead. SUB gets the most aggressive weights since instruction substitution is nearly free and directly obscures the arithmetic that dominates these kernels; BCF stays high because its cost is mostly static size, which this very small binary can easily absorb, while its runtime cost is near zero with well-formed opaque predicates. FLA keeps the highest SecurityGain (flattening is the strongest structural deterrent for search/recursion logic) but carries the largest RuntimeCost and CorrectnessRisk weights so the selector spares the deepest recursive hot paths and avoids miscompilation risk; SPLIT is kept as a cheap diversity amplifier that composes well with FLA by giving it more basic blocks to flatten. IBR and ICALL get solid security/diversity weights with moderate costs since indirect branching and calls cheaply break static call-graph recovery, which is high-value against reverse engineering of a program whose structure (game search) is otherwise easy to recognize. IGV is included but with the highest SizeCost weight, since global-variable indirection adds data-section growth with less benefit for a program with few globals and no meaningful static data to hide.
